issue_context.summary: Display reconfiguration correlates with a kernel stack-recursion crash only while Always On Top is enabled, but current-build confirmation is outstanding.
known_information: Three dumps reportedly show 0x7F parameter 8 and win32kbase PDEV recursion.
The scenario uses two high-refresh DisplayPort monitors and repeated sleep/lock/power cycling.
Disabling Always On Top stopped recurrence.
FancyZones was disabled; Windhawk taskbar modules were installed.
inferences: Always On Top event activity may be a trigger, but a user-mode module does not establish kernel root cause.
Display driver, shell modification, and OS interactions remain plausible.
issue_context.analysis: The crash evidence is useful, but repeating the active author request would be noise. Preserve waiting status.
initial_investigation: AlwaysOnTop.cpp installs out-of-context WinEvent hooks for location, minimize, move/size, foreground, destroy, and focus.
Recent history has rendering/shutdown changes but no linked fix or duplicate for this signature.
No assignee or maintainer reproduction exists.
